docs.title: Common
docs.text:
You need to do this no matter what

  • Run POI(Brave stopped supporting V2 manifest too... farewell KC3) with debug mode
  • Use task manager to kill all POI process if needed. This debug instance of POI must be the first instance for POI to run. If you have other POI windows open, close all of them before re-starting with remote-debugging enabled.
  • Example: poi --remote-debugging-port=9222 --remote-allow-origins=* (For Windows user: If you don't know how to start POI with options, read this) (--remote-allow-origins=* is needed at the moment (2023/05/04)ref):

  • How do I know if the debug mode is on?

    • Access 127.0.0.1:9222, you should see a blank screen as follow:
    • Kill ALL POI process and retry if you see this:

  • Install plugin poi-plugin-noro6-exporter and poi-plugin-forwarder

  • For Linux(Ubuntu) users: Wayland in Ubuntu does not work well with kcauto(and a lot of other stuffs, lol) You would want to run your Ubuntu with the good old X-windows

docs.title: Start Up
docs.text: Pick one from Beginner, Gamer or Developer

docs.title: Beginner
docs.text:
You have limited features but easiest installation and setup.

  • Windows
    • Double click kcauto_cui.exe
  • Linux
    • Run ./kcauto_cui

That's it!

docs.title: Gamer
docs.text:
You have to deal with Noro6 but full access to all features.

  • Windows
    • run .\kcauto_cui.exe in Powershell for better user experience
    • or, run .\kcauto_custom.exe --cfg <your_config_name> to specify your own config file (note that you do not need to add .json here)
  • Linux
    • Run ./kcauto_cui
    • or, run ./kcauto.bin --cfg <your_config_name> to specify your own config file (note that you do not need to add .json here)

docs.title: Expert
docs.text:
Tweak everything from config file like a pro. Not for kid.

Always keep your backup. Do not join if you don't know what you're doing.

See Ch4 for detail

docs.title: Developer
docs.text:
Your own Python environment, free to edit/fix the tool yourself.

  • Install Python 3.11 and pip
  • Install pipenv using pip install pipenv
  • Create your .venv, quick ref if you forgot how to make one
  • Activate venv by source .venv/bin/activate
  • Install dependencies:
  • pip install -r requirements.txt

  • Check requirements.txt for more instructions if you find yourself missing library

  • Windows

    • run python .\kcauto\kcauto_cui.py
    • or, run python kcauto --cfg <your_config_name> to specify your own config file (note that you do not need to add .json here)
  • Linux
    • Run python3 ./kcauto/kcauto_cui.py
    • or, run python3 kcauto --cfg <your_config_name> to specify your own config file (note that you do not need to add .json here)

docs.title: On your first run, you would need to start kcauto in splash screen
docs.text:
Select log panel, and reload your config.

You might get hit by the following error on the first run:

[SUCCESS][2026-02-23 17:35:36] Initializing kcauto.
[DEBUG][2026-02-23 17:35:36] Loading data from 'configs/config_cui.json'.
[DEBUG][2026-02-23 17:35:36] Loading data from 'data/config/config_cui_template.json'.
[DEBUG][2026-02-23 17:35:36] Combat config init called
[DEBUG][2026-02-23 17:35:36] SET _sortie_map_read_only: {MapEnum(value)}
[DEBUG][2026-02-23 17:35:36] _repair_bucket_threshold set 500
[SUCCESS][2026-02-23 17:35:36] Config successfully loaded.
[DEBUG][2026-02-23 17:35:36] Loading data from 'data/temp/reinforce_general_category.json'.
[ERROR][2026-02-23 17:35:36] Reinforce equipment data not found, please start kcauto from splash screen
[ERROR][2026-02-23 17:35:36] [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'data/temp/reinforce_general_category.json'
[DEBUG][2026-02-23 17:35:36] Loading data from 'data/temp/equipment_list.json'.
[ERROR][2026-02-23 17:35:36] Equipment data not found, please start kcauto from splash screen
[ERROR][2026-02-23 17:35:36] [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'data/temp/equipment_list.json'

This is because kcauto_custom has never get the data it needs from kancolle. As long as your data/temp folder is fill with the following files after the first run, you are fine and can simply run kcauto_custom for second time.

All the temp files kcauto_custom acquire from kancolle

For Windows user: There are reports show that kcauto_custom does not work well with chrome_driver mode on Windows. If you are having issue on mouse control, it is recommended to switch to direct_control mode.

How to: 1. Run kcauto_custom once 2. Close kcauto_custom 3. Open configs/config_cui.json 4. Edit "general.interaction_mode": "chrome_driver", => "general.interaction_mode": "direct_control", 5. Save and close

Windows mouse issue should be fixed in latest version.(2026/07/28)

docs.title: Ch3.1: Sortie
docs.text: No pain, no gain

docs.title: Overview -- Sortie mode: Auto
docs.text:
In short, Sortie mode: Auto could finish daily, weekly and monthly quests fully automated

It brings you a highly automated experience:

  1. kcauto-custom picks an available quest for you
  2. It loads the preset you defined in Noro6
  3. It sorties to the map which requested from the quest

Setup your combat fleets in noro6

On the other hand, the setup is a bit more complicated, you will have to setup a few things in Noro6 and kcauto_custom

  1. map and quest id: What map does this fleet(編成) file setup for(ex. is it for 1-5? or 6-3 from Bq4?)
  2. Ship and equipment: What ship and equipment to use
  3. Quest pool: What quest you want to do

With that said, let's begin~

docs.title: Noro6
docs.text:
I mean... it's obvious we need this, right?

Noro6 is a great simulator and you can import your ship & equipment pool to setup your own fleet.

More on that later.

docs.title: Config setup
docs.text:
There are three steps to setup your noro6 config file, a template is located in configs/noro6/noro6:

  1. Export your ship and equipment to noro6
  2. Create your noro6 config
  3. Import the noro6 config to kcauto_custom

docs.title: Exporting
docs.text:
Let's start with exporting your own ship and equipment to noro6 Well it's kinda simple,

Open Noro6 Exporter

Click export to Noro6

Your are automatically switched to noro6!

Now click setting, then import the tutorial in "configs/noro6/noro6_template"

That's it, we are done!

docs.title: Setting up config
docs.text:
Next step, we are going to edit a fleet config

Let's open B-1-1

Ummmm... What can I say? Just set up your fleet and equipment here, don't forget to save I guess? There will be lots of configs to setup, the clipboard function in noro6 is a life saver.

setup fleet in noro6

clipboard function could save you effort

docs.title: Import to kcauto_custom
docs.text: Click setting => Create backup file => Overwrite the configs/noro6/noro6 template, that's it.

docs.title: Sortie mode: Auto test run
docs.text:
After you setup B-1-1 config, you can use this from kcauto_cui

That's it, let's try it out!

docs.title: Put together your own sortie noro6 config
docs.text:
The B-1-1 is a huge step, but that alone doesn't do much. Now you want to create noro6 configs as needed, here are things to be aware of:

  1. The file name of every fleet config must be B<quest_id>-<world>-<stage>-<target_node>. For example, B-1-1 is the config made for 1-1, By6-1-2 is the config specially made for 1-2 in quest By6, B-7-2-G is the config made for 7-2-G.
  2. You can assign both ships and equipment in a config.
  3. LBAS (Land-Based Air Squadrons) assign is sadly NOT supported yet.
  4. If a quest specify config is not found(ex. By6-1-2), kcauto_custom would fall back to normal config (ex. B-1-2)
  5. Feel free to add your own config (I am sure I've missed quite a few quest related configs)
  6. If you're too lazy to finish all the configs at once, REMOVE those you didn't setup, or kcauto_custom would get confuse

There is a template at configs/noro6/noro6_template to save you some naming time if you want to finish your setup in once You do have to remove those unuse config if you decide to start from this template

An example of configs

docs.title: Use Sortie mode: Auto in kcauto_cui
docs.text: After finishing all config you need, you can use this from kcauto_cui

docs.title: Ch3.2: Expedition
docs.text: Humanity is acquiring all the right technology for all the wrong reasons.

docs.title: Overview -- Expedition mode: Auto
docs.text:
Expedition mode: Auto is a fully automated expedition mode, it is capable to:

  1. Assign ships to form a valid fleet for specific expedition
  2. Balance player's resources by picking the most efficient expedition
  3. Handle Landing Craft and Drum Canisters requirements
  4. Load fleets in Noro6 config if provided (See section Noro6)

A simplified overview of Expedition mode: Auto

docs.title: Ship pool
docs.text:
Same as combat module, ship pool is defined in ship_pool.json. You will have to set this up yourself.

No, you don't have to set up the ship pool anymore Any ship which matches ALL in the following:

  1. NOT assigned in ANY config in Noro6
  2. Locked

Are automatically assigned to EXP ship pool

How expedition ship pool is defined

docs.title: Noro6
docs.text: For combat expedition(ex. A5, A6) or expedition require ships occupied by Noro6 already, you can define an expedition Noro6 config so kcauto can still run those expeditions.

docs.title: This only works when sortie and PvP are both disabled,
docs.text:
since all Noro6 configs share the same ship and equipment pool

Example of expedition Noro6 config

docs.title: Setting up config
docs.text:
Example file name for expedition config

Things to be aware of:

  1. The file name of every expedition config must be D-<Expedition ID>. For example, D-A3 is the config made for A3,
  2. You can assign both ships and equipment in a config.
  3. Noro6 config has priority over kcauto_custom's auto assigned fleet
  4. Again, expedition which reference Noro6 only works when sortie and PvP are both disabled, since all Noro6 configs share the same ship and equipment pool
  5. Feel free to add your own config

The general idea is the same as sortie noro6 config in Ch3.1

docs.title: Ship assign
docs.text:
You can enable ship assign by selecting auto.

It's been a while but this is not an early version of expedition mode: auto anymore. expedition mode: auto now :

  1. Does handle Level requirement
  2. Does handle Drum Canister and landing crafts bonus requirement
  3. Does handle expeditions like A1, B6 etc. (with the help from Noro6)
  4. Expedition set is pick on fly, not on startup only anymore
  5. Fleet switch would happens on whichever idle fleet, without the need of waiting for all fleets to return

docs.title: Ch3.3: PvP
docs.text: Humanity is acquiring all the right technology for all the wrong reasons.

docs.title: Overview -- PvP mode: Auto
docs.text:
PvP mode: Auto follow the same principle as sortie mode: Auto and expedition mode: Auto, it finish PvP quests automatically:

  1. User can setup fleet presets in Noro6
  2. kcauto_custom pick a PvP quest
  3. kcauto_custom load the corresponding fleet and attempt to finish the quest

docs.title: PvP quest handling
docs.text:
To prevent kcauto_custom from selecting every available PvP quest, kcauto_custom now has the ability to judge if the fleet matches the requirement of a quest.

For example, if the fleet doesn't has 1CL+3DD or 4DD, kcauto_custom would not select the quest Cq4 (小艦艇群演習強化任務). Or a warning will be sent if kcauto_custom is forced to attempt to finish this quest.

Warning message for non valid fleet

docs.title: Noro6
docs.text:
Here are things to be aware of:

  1. The file name of every PvP config must be C<quest id>-pvp. For example, Cm2-pvp is the config made for quest Cm2,
  2. You can assign both ships and equipment in a config.
  3. Feel free to add your own config

Example PvP config name

docs.title: Ch4.1: Sortie
docs.text: We're all nerds, on one subject or another.

docs.title: Before you read
docs.text: There is a User config wiki page in Ch5 Configuration File You can find the explain for each option in user config Check that out if you find yourself surrounded by unknown terms

docs.title: Map specified Sortie setting (combat.override)
docs.text:
In most cases, kcauto_custom sortie with the same general logic.

  • Diamond for anti-air
  • Line Abreast for anti-sub
  • Vanguard instead of Line Ahead during event
  • Get into night battle against boss for rank S result
  • etc.

Though in some others maps, we do need to:

  • Select node (ex. In 5-3, we select node K to node O)
  • Setup lbas (ex. In 6-4, 6-5, 7-4 etc.)
  • Attempt using Nelson touch
  • Attempt using smoke
  • etc.

Issue is those settings are not gonna work for other maps, and the map specified setting is here to help.

docs.title: What if I don't need this?
docs.text:
Set combat.override in your config to true. Your kcauto works the same as before.

There are 3 levels of Sortie settings:

  1. User config(Your normal config, configs/config_cui.json if you're using CUI)
  2. Default data/config/combat/default.json (Default sortie config for general map)
  3. Map specified setting (ex.data/config/combat/B-4-5.json)(Sortie config made for specific map)

The priority here is User config < Default < Map specified And you can define enabled, fleet_presets and sortie_map from User config ONLY(show as STATIC in the following pic).

Feel free to edit or add configs under data/config/combat. As long as combat.override in your own config is set to false, kcauto will read the corresponding setting automatically.

docs.title: Sortie mode: Auto -- quest handling
docs.text:
Before you read: Usually you don't need to set this up yourself if you are using the CUI. Do NOT edit the files here if you're not sure what you're doing

Now we have told kcauto-custom what ship to use, but how do kcauto-custom pick a map and finish quests for me?

There are 3 files that would affect the behavior of quest & map picking (usually you don't have to edit them):

  1. Your config file (config/config_cui.json for cui user)
  2. data/quest/quest.json
  3. data/quest/quest_priority.json

Let's take a look into the config file first:

    "quest.enabled":    true,       #Enable the quest module
    "quest.quests": ["Bd1", "Bd2", "Bd3", "Bd4", "Bd5", "Bd6", "Bd7", "Bd8", "Bw1", "Bw2", "Bw3", "Bw4", "Bw5", "Bw7", "Bw8", "Bw9", "Bw10", "Bm2", "Bm3", "Bm4", "Bm5", "Bm6", "Bm8", "Bq1", "Bq3", "Bq4", "Bq8", "Bq9", "Bq10", "Bq11", "Bq12", "C2", "C3", "C4", "C8", "C16", "C29", "D2", "D3", "D4", "D9", "D11", "D22", "D24", "E3", "E4", "F5", "F6", "F7", "F8"]
    # The quests that kcauto-custom will attempt to finish

kcauto-custom will only handle the quests mentioned in quest.quests.

Next one is data/quest/quest.json, this file contains the details of a quest. Again, usually you wouldn't want to edit it.


  "Bd1": {                         #The quest name
    "id": 201,                     #The quest ID
    "type": "daily",               #The quest type
    "intervals": [1, 0, 0],        #Intervals between kcauto-custom checking if the quest is finished, with the order as [sortie, pvp, expedition]
    "recommended_map": ["1-1"]     #The map which kcauto-custom will sortie to if no info could gather from KC3
  }

The last one is data/quests/sorite_quest_priority.json, it defines what quest kcauto-costom will prioritizes when user is in Sortie mode: Auto

{

  "time_limited": [
    "2412B5",
    "2509B5"
  ],
  "exact_ship_and_map": [
    "Bm1",
   ．．．
    "By15"
  ],
  "exact_ship_type_and_map": [
    "Bm3",
．．．
    "By11"
  ],
  "any_ship_with_exact_map": [
    "Bm8",
．．．
    "Bq10"
  ],
  "exact_area": [
    "Bw6",
    "Bw7"
  ],
  "exact_enemy_type": [
    "Bw2",
．．．
    "Bw3"
  ],
  "any_sortie": [
    "Bd1",
．．．
    "Bw1"
  ],
  "low_priority": [
    "Bd7"
  ]
}

The priority here is daily > weekly > monthly > quarterly > yearly > low_priority

docs.title: Ch4.2: Factory
docs.text: Standardization, not perfection, is the key to scale.

docs.title: Factory recipe preset
docs.text:
To avoid wiki-ing every time when changing recipe. kcauto_custom is capable to read recipe preset in JSON format.

The files are data/factory/construct_recipe_preset.json and data/factory/develop_recipe_preset.json. The format is:

    <preset name>: {
        "factory.build_recipe": [
            <fuel>,
            <ammo>,
            <steel>,
            <bauxite>
        ],
        "factory.build_secretary": <ship id>
    }

    <preset name>: {
        "factory.develop_recipe": [
            <fuel>,
            <ammo>,
            <steel>,
            <bauxite>
        ],
        "factory.develop_secretary": <ship id>
    }

Format of construct and develop recipe preset

{
    "Daily": {
        "factory.build_recipe": [
            30,
            30,
            30,
            30
        ],
        "factory.build_secretary": 0
    },
    "まるゆ": {
        "factory.build_recipe": [
            1500,
            1500,
            2000,
            1000
        ],
        "factory.build_secretary": 0
    }
}

{
    "radar": {
        "factory.develop_recipe": [
            10,
            10,
            250,
            250
        ],
        "factory.develop_secretary": 456
    },
    "91-AP": {
        "factory.develop_recipe": [
            10,
            30,
            90,
            10
        ],
        "factory.develop_secretary": 123
    }
}

Example of construct and develop recipe preset

The preset will appear on the left of factory panel after you setup the above files. Simply selecting it will apply the corresponding recipe.

Example of applying recipe preset

docs.title: Ch5: Configuration File
docs.text: Out of clutter, find simplicity.

docs.title: Config setting flow
docs.text:
kcauto_custom is basically a standalone program runs with a config file.

The CUI(Command line User Interface) we use is just a config file editor, it makes kcauto_custom easier to use, but it is not a must.

You can for sure edit the config file with notepad and runs kcauto_custom with it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
KCAuto uses JSON configuration files to control its behavior. The configuration system is modular, with different sections controlling different aspects of the automation.

All configuration files must be valid JSON format.

docs.title: File Format
docs.text: Configuration files are JSON objects with dot-notation keys. Each key follows the pattern <module>.<setting>.

docs.title: Example Basic Structure
docs.text:
{
    "general.interaction_mode": "chrome_driver",
    "general.jst_offset": 0,
    "combat.enabled": true,
    "combat.sortie_map": "1-1",
    "expedition.enabled": false
}

docs.title: General Settings (general.*)
docs.text: Controls basic application behavior and browser interaction.

docs.title: general.interaction_mode
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Valid Values: "chrome_driver", "direct_control"
  • Default: "chrome_driver"
  • Description: Determines how kcauto interacts with the browser. Chrome driver mode sends control signal to browser directly, while direct control mode control your mouse to interact with browser.

docs.title: general.jst_offset
docs.text:
• Type: integer
  • Valid Range: -20 to 20
  • Default: 0
  • Description: Time offset in hours from JST (Japan Standard Time) for scheduling and time-based operations.

docs.title: general.chrome_dev_port
docs.text:
• Type: integer
  • Valid Range: 0 to 65535
  • Default: 9222
  • Description: Port number for Chrome DevTools Protocol connection. Do not change if you don't know what you're doing.

docs.title: general.poi_api_port
docs.text:
• Type: integer
  • Valid Range: 0 to 65535
  • Default: 9223
  • Description: Port number for POI API forwarding. Do not change if you don't know what you're doing.

docs.title: general.paused Not working at the moment(2025/07/17)
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: false
  • Description: Whether kcauto should start in paused state.

docs.title: Combat Settings (combat.*)
docs.text: Controls sortie and combat behavior.

docs.title: combat.enabled
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: false
  • Description: Enables or disables the combat module entirely.

docs.title: combat.sortie_map
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Valid Format: Map notation like "1-1", "3-5", "6-4", or "auto"
  • Default: "1-1"
  • Description: Specifies which map to sortie to. Use "auto" for automatic map selection.
  • Example: "1-1", "3-5", "E-1", "auto"

docs.title: combat.fleet_mode
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Valid Values: "standard", "strike", "tcf", "ctf", "stf"
  • Default: "standard"
  • Description: Defines the fleet formation mode for combat.
  • "standard": Single fleet
  • "strike": Strike force (uses fleet 3)
  • "tcf": Transport Combined Fleet
  • "ctf": Carrier Task Force
  • "stf": Surface Task Force

docs.title: combat.fleet_presets
docs.text:
• Type: array of integers or strings
  • Valid Values: Numbers 1-15 or "auto"
  • Default: []
  • Description: List of fleet preset numbers to use for combat. Use "auto" for automatic fleet selection.
  • Example: [1, 2, 3], ["auto"]

docs.title: combat.check_fatigue
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: true
  • Description: Whether kcauto should check ship fatigue levels during combat operations.

docs.title: combat.check_lbas_fatigue
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: true
  • Description: Whether kcauto should check Land-Based Air Squadron (LBAS) fatigue during combat.

docs.title: combat.clear_stop
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: false
  • Description: Whether kcauto should stop combat operations when the map has been cleared.

docs.title: combat.port_check
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: false
  • Description: Whether to check port capacity before sorties.

docs.title: combat.reserve_repair_dock
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: true
  • Description: Whether to reserve repair dock slots for emergency repairs.

docs.title: combat.retreat_limit
docs.text:
• Type: integer
  • Valid Values: 0-4 (damage state levels)
  • Default: 4
  • Description: Damage threshold for retreating ships. Values correspond to damage states:
  • 0: No damage
  • 1: Scratch damage
  • 2: Minor damage
  • 3: Moderate damage
  • 4: Heavy damage

docs.title: combat.repair_limit
docs.text:
• Type: integer

docs.title: Ch99.1: Your own event map support
Appendix ‐‐ Making your own event map support
docs.text:
The lazy author takes forever to update event support How about making your own event update pack?

~Warning: If you don't have your own kcauto python environment, then it is highly impossible for you to make your own update pack(since you have no access to kcauto/kca_enums/nodes.py)~ (2025/11/12, with the latest update, nodes define are separated to data/combat/map_enum.json, so normal user should be able to follow this guide now)

There are three things to setup: 1. assets (assets/combat/_event_next_page_<X>.png and assets/combat/_event_world_E-<X>.png) 2. map data (data/combat/E-<X>.json) 3. nodes (data/combat/map_enum.json)

docs.title: Assets
docs.text:
For assets, you have to capture ref of the map icon FROM TO

And the next page button FROM 

LOL, can't find the original pic at the moment
It's the big red triangle next page button on the right

TO

Then replace the files in assets/combat/_event_next_page_<X>.png and assets/combat/_event_world_E-<X>.png

docs.title: map data
docs.text:
Now we have to setup the map data so that kcauto can handle combat and LBAS for us. First thing first, we need to get the map image ready. I personally get it from kancolle wiki We need the image without any scaling so be careful with the source you use.

Where you can get reliable map image

A mini tool tool/mapCoorUpdater.py could help building up the map data, the requirement to run this python file is listed in tool/mapCoorUpdaterRequirement.txt.

Run the tool and it will pull the latest map edges data from KC3 source code. So make sure you work on this after KC3 has updated the event map data.

Map Coordinates Updater

After you finished filling in basic info, the coor of each node is needed to be defined (ref:issue#20 and discussion#71): 1. Click top left of the map 2. Follow the guide from the tool and set the node type if needed (press o for option node, a for anti-air node, s for anti-sub node, b for boss node) 3. click on each node

Set node C as option node

Where to click on the image

mapCoorUpdater finished setting up E-4.json

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text:
In order for kcauto to handle, all nodes are defined in data/combat/map_enum.json.

You don't have to add the newly updated nodes into the file manually, tho. Run tool/maps_generater.py and it will generate tool/map_enum.json. then replace data/combat/map_enum.json with tool/map_enum.json.

docs.title: Debugging map data
docs.text:
In case you need to debug a E-X.json file, Let's take a look in a old E-5.json. Map data defines the node, edge, and enemy type in a map.

= json { "world": "E", //This is an event map "subworld": 5, //The 5th world "panel": 1, //It is located at the 1st panel (The upper one), this is needed because for example E1~E3 could all located at page 1 "page": 3, //It is located at 3rd page "enemy_context": [ //What type of enemy will appear in this map, these data will then provide to quest module "subs", "carriers", "transports" ], "nodes": { //Coords for every nodes, this is the offset from top left of the GAME WINDOW(not your browser or screen) to the node "A": { "coords": [ 157, 273 ] }, ... ... "L2": { "coords": [ 775, 424 ] } }, "edges": { //The edge between every nodes, this is defined in the api from kancolle "1": [ "Start 1", "A" ], ... ... "37": [ "V", "U" ] } }

docs.title: Ch99.2: Your own (time limit) quest
docs.text: My laziness has reached a new level.

docs.title: Appendix ‐‐ Making your own (time limit) quest
docs.text:
With this article, you will be able to add any Sortie, PvP or Expedition quest yourself.

To define a new quest for kcauto_custom, you'll need to provide: 1. Quest info 2. Quest requirement 3. Quest specify Noro6 tag (if needed) 4. Quest priority

Which are handled by the following files: 1. data/quests/kc3_quests_en.json 2. data/quests/quests.json 3. data/combat/map_enum.json 4. data/quests/<type>_quest_priority.json

docs.title: Quest info -- kc3_quests_en
docs.text:
As the name suggested, this file comes from KC3, you can find the file here and simply copy&paste, be aware it usually takes a few days for KC3's dev to update latest quests.

This file provide the basic quest info used by CUI and the quest id we will need later.

Quest info comes from KC3

docs.title: Quest requirement -- quests.json
docs.text:
Now we define the quest in quest.json, this file contains the details of a quest. You can always take a look in other quests in data/quests/quests.json if you need any examples. ```json! "1234B1": { #The quest name, copy from kc3_quests_en "id": 999, #The quest id, copy from kc3_quests_en "type": "weekly", #The quest type, valid values are "daily", "weekly", "monthly", "other" "recommended_map": [ #(sortie only) The map which kcauto-custom will sortie to "1234B1-1-1", "1234B1-1-2", "1234B1-1-3" ], "expedition_context": [ #(expedition only) The expedition which kcauto-custom will head to 29, 30, 131, 133 ] "intervals": [1, 0, 0], #(optional) Intervals between kcauto-custom checking if the quest is finished, with the order as [sortie, pvp, expedition], "fleet_composition": {...} #(optional) The fleet requirement of this quest },


#### a. quest name

You can find the quest name by selecting the quest and hop over in KC3 panel,  
for example, the following time limit PvP quest is `2507C1`

<img width="393" height="80" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09e6a21c-951d-4d5a-a1bd-b58ebd397a4a" />

#### b. quest id

Open `data/quests/kc3_quests_en.json`,  search for quest name above,  
you will find the quest id, we will use "2507C1" as example.

... "380": { <= the id we are looking for "code": "2507C1", "name": "Weekly [Time-limited] Landing Fleet Escort Exercises!", "desc": "Secure 3 A-Rank+ victories in Exercises within the same day using either an LHA and 2 DE OR 3 DE, and up to 3 additional ships.", "memo": "\u27a3Rewards:\n\u00B6First choice: Either three Buckets OR a Screw OR a Combat Ration\n\u00B6Second choice: Either three Development Materials OR two Type 94 Depth Charge Projectors OR a Type 3 Depth Charge Projector" }, ...


#### c. quest type

The tab of which this quest belongs to, valid values are "daily", "weekly", "monthly", "other"

#### d. recommended_map (**Sortie quest only**)

Shows the map which kcauto-custom will sortie to.  
The naming rule is simple, `"<quest name>-<map>"`  
For example, quest `2509B5` require S-rank in `4-2`, `4-3`, `4-4`:

"recommended_map": [
  "2509B5-4-2",
  "2509B5-4-3",
  "2509B5-4-4"
]


#### e. expedition_context (**Expedition quest only**)

Shows the expedition id which kcauto-custom will head to.  
You can find expedition ID for A1, B2 etc. in [`kcauto/kca_enums/expeditions.py`](https://github.com/XVs32/kcauto_custom/blob/develop/kcauto/kca_enums/expeditions.py)  
For example, quest `Dy7` require expedition to `29`, `30`, `D1`, `D3`:

"expedition_context": [      
  29,
  30,
  131,
  133
]


#### f. fleet_composition (optional, not suggested)

This item shows the fleet requirement of the quest,  
if the current fleet does not match the requirement here,  
kcauto_custom would not apply for this quest, which means quest slots are use more wisely.  

However, it is more complicate to setup that I would say it does not worth it in time limit quest,  
you could find the detail definition in [`reference/fleet_composition_documentation.md`](https://github.com/XVs32/kcauto_custom/blob/develop/reference/fleet_composition_documentation.md).    

"fleet_composition": {...}     #(optional) The fleet requirement of this quest


---

### Noro6 tag -- map_enum.json (**Sortie quest only**)

**This step is only needed when this is a sortie quest,  
AND when you do need a dedicate noro6 config for this quest.**

`map_enum.json` contains all the sortie map kcauto_custom would handle,  
this is also the name tag for every sortie noro6 config.  
If you added maps in `recommended_map` above, you will need to add it here too.  

The naming rule is simple,  
`"W<map>-<quest name>" : "<quest name>-<map>"`
For example:

"W2_2_A": "B-2-2-A",
"W6_4": "B-6-4",
"W2_5_Bm1": "Bm1-2-5",
"W4-4-2509B5": "2509B5-4-4",
"W2-3-2412B5": "2412B5-2-3",


---

### quest_priority

The last one is ```data/quests/<type>_quest_priority.json```, it defines what quest kcauto-costom will prioritizes over the others: 

Naming does not matter and the priority sort in descend order. ( "2412B5" > "2509B5" > "Bm1" ... etc.)

```json!
{

  "time_limited": [
    "2412B5",
    "2509B5"
  ],
  "exact_ship_and_map": [
    "Bm1",
   ．．．
    "By15"
  ],
  "exact_ship_type_and_map": [
    "Bm3",
．．．
    "By11"
  ],
  "any_ship_with_exact_map": [
    "Bm8",
．．．
    "Bq10"
  ],
  "exact_area": [
    "Bw6",
    "Bw7"
  ],
  "exact_enemy_type": [
    "Bw2",
．．．
    "Bw3"
  ],
  "any_sortie": [
    "Bd1",
．．．
    "Bw1"
  ],
  "low_priority": [
    "Bd7"
  ]
}

docs.title: Appendix ‐‐ Noro6 equipment update
docs.text:
Since Noro6 doesn't get update after you upgrade an equipment, after time you will get spam by the following warning:

This article provides the usage of an semi-auto script in kcauto_custom's tool box, which is meant to saves you effort from updating Noro6's equipment data manually.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The idea of this script is to automatically click the update button for each config in noro6, so that you're sync with the equipment you have in stock.

Equipment update function in Noro6

docs.title: Updating equipment data

First we need to grab the latest data from KC3

Exporting data from KC3

You would want to turn on auto save in setting panel so that every file is saved after the script finished it's job.

Auto save option in Noro6

Console panel in browser

The script is locate in develop/tool/noro6_equipment_update.js, copy & paste the code into console panel, press Enter to run.

const isVisible = (el) => {
    if (!el) return false;
    const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);

...

}

runTurboAutomation();

docs.text:
Warnning : Althought kcauto_custom could theoretically run on Windows, it was originally made for Linux, I might or might not fix any compatibility issues.

kcauto_custom is a customized version of an archived project kcauto that includes additional features and functionality. In comparison with kcauto, kcauto_custom is less flexible while being more automatic for easy daily use. Executable file is provided for those don't want to build their own python env. User can setup their fleet and equipment configuration in Noro6, then excute the plan with kcauto_custom. This tool is designed to help users automate repetitive tasks such as Expedition, Combat, PvP, Repair & Resupply, ultimately saving time and improving efficiency.

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text:
kcauto_custom is meant for educational purposes only. Botting is against the rules and prolonged usage of kcauto_custom may result in your account being banned. The developer of kcauto_custom takes no responsibility for repercussions related to the usage of kcauto_custom. You have been warned!

Although unlikely, users may lose ships and equipment when using kcauto_custom to conduct combat sorties. While kcauto_custom has been painstakingly designed to reduce the chances of this happening, the developer of kcauto_custom does not take responsibility for any loss of ships and/or resources.

docs.title: Original features form kcauto
docs.text:
• Expedition — automate expeditions
  • PvP Module — automate PvP
  • Combat Module — automate combat sorties
  • LBAS Module — automatic LBAS management
  • Ship Switcher Module — automatic switching of ships based on specified criteria between combat sorties
  • Fleet Switcher Module — automatic switching of fleet presets for PvP and combat sorties
  • Quests Module — automatic quest management
  • Repair & Resupply Modules — automatic resupply and repair of fleet ships
  • Stats — keeps stats on various actions performed
  • Click Tracking — optional tracking of clicks done by kcauto
  • Scheduled and manual sleeping and pausing of individual modules or entire script
  • Automatic catbomb and script recovery
  • Random variations in navigation, timers, and click positions to combat bot detection

docs.title: Features form kcauto_custom
docs.text:
• Executable file — No more Python struggle
  • CUI(Character User Interface) for daily use cases
  • Akashi repair Module — Repair ships with akashi
  • Factory Module — Runs daily develop and ship building

  • Support for 7-4, events
